summary: Speckled grey, pink and white granite polished to a countertop shine.
_comment: Polished granite: a speckled grey, pink and white coarse-grained igneous stone, ground and polished to a near-mirror countertop finish (ambientCG Granite001A, CC0, its polished 'A' variant; roughness map mean 0.05). Opaque: a solid dielectric; granite does not scatter light through like marble. The source states no physical size: the scan is 0.4 m by a judgement from the grain size (crystals of about 3-5 mm span 7-13 px of its 1024 px tile). Re-made at its tag (2026-10-16, Phase19 D-9): the maps are quilted from the scan into an exact 1 m tile (tools/converters/base/quilt_scan.py), every patch at the scan's own size, its broad pale streak flattened first so it does not repeat; written at 2048 px. Nothing stretched. Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): scratches (overlay 1, damage), dust as a deposit (Phase10), water spots, gated by the Crevice mask. Built by the Phase11 batch.
name: Granite_Polished_Clean_Base_s1_v01

sources.why: re-makes the scan at its scale option: quilted at the scan's own size, never stretched

specular_ior 1.54, that of quartz (Physically Based 'Quartz'), granite's main mineral with feldspar (about 1.52-1.53); Physically Based has no granite entry. The scan's 0.4 m from the grain size, since the source states no physical size; the article tiles at exactly 1 m (quilted).
